10.0.0.en: "Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain; so the LORD shall make lightnings, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field." [1].

10.0.1.en: In ancient times, because of evil, Elijah stopped the rain for three years and six months so that all might be disciplined and the rain come down; so our sins withhold the abundant overflow of God's graces upon us and deprive us of His rain, which turns the barren wilderness into a garden that gladdens His heart (Song 5:1).

10.0.2.en: In our study of the book of Hosea (6:3) we observed that in Palestine an early rain falls when the seed is sown, and a latter rain by which the harvest ripens. The first rain signifies the work of the Holy Spirit through the Law and the prophecies, etc., before the coming of the Lord, while the latter signifies the overflowing descent of the Holy Spirit upon the Church of the New Testament, which was announced by the prophet Joel: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28).

10.0.3.en: We may say that the early rain is the Law and the prophecies which the Lord granted to the men of the Old Testament, while the latter rain is the preaching of the Gospel, which reveals the mysteries of God and gives us a deep knowledge and a vision of the divine life.

10.0.4.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the early rain also means the teachings concerning the incarnation of the Savior, while the latter rain is the enjoyment of the mysteries of His divinity.

10.0.5.en: In any case, let us not cease to ask God without interruption that He may flash lightning in our hearts with the splendour of His glory, granting us His latter rain to water our land with His divine love and give it abundant fruit.

10.1.0.en: 2 For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd. 3 "Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the he-goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle.

10.1.1.en: Although God sends rain on the good and the wicked, He gives the spiritual rain only to those who ask for it. And now, in order that He may take care of His flock spiritually, this flock must leave the deceptions of divination, sorcery, and the dreams of the false prophets, so that He Himself may shepherd His people.

10.1.2.en: "For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd. Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the he-goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle" [2-3].

10.1.3.en: The teraphim are images of gods which they set up inside their houses as guardians for them and to consult before every action. God cannot take over the shepherding of His people so long as they rely on the teraphim, ask the diviners, and resort to the dreams of the false prophets, for all these may flatter a man and deceive him with soft, deceptive words, but those who rely on them do not fall into abasement, since they are without care. Now, when the people leave these vain deceptions, the Lord does two things: He declares His anger against the corrupt shepherds and takes over the shepherding Himself, as He affirmed in the book of Ezekiel: "Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out... I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord GOD" (Ezek 34:11, 15). He punishes the wicked he-goats (the rams) and takes care of His flock, giving His life as a ransom for them (Jn 10:11). He gives them His life, able to make them like a horse in the procession of salvation, able to fight against the devil and his works. As it was said: "Was the LORD displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers, or thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?" (Hab 3:8).

10.2.s.en: 3. Enjoying victory and the restoration of the kingdom:

10.2.0.en: 4 Out of him came forth the corner, out of him the nail, out of him the battle bow, out of him every oppressor together. 5 And they shall be as mighty men, which tread down their enemies in the mire of the streets in the battle: and they shall fight, because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses shall be confounded. 6 And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the LORD their God, and will hear them. 7 And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad; their heart shall rejoice in the LORD. 8 I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them: and they shall increase as they have increased. 9 And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again. 10 I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them. 11 And he shall pass through the sea with affliction, and shall smite the waves in the sea, and all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away. 12 And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the LORD."

10.2.1.en: The fruit of God's personal care is that they enjoy victory, security, joy, and the restoration of God's kingdom among them.

10.2.2.en: First: "Out of him came forth the corner, out of him the nail, out of him the battle bow, out of him every oppressor speedily" [4]. True divine care appears in the manifestation of the Lord Christ in the midst of His people as a cornerstone who binds all together in Him and supports all with one Spirit. He also appears among them as a nail that supports their temporal tent, that is, their temporary life, so that the winds of strange teachings and the storms of the love of the world and the lusts of the flesh do not move it. This is the divine nail that supports the body (the tent) by sanctifying it for the sake of the Kingdom of God. And the Lord is also among them a battle bow which the believer aims, fighting evil and sin, so that it is said of them: "One of you shall chase a thousand, and two shall put ten thousand to flight" (Deut 32:30); and they are as soldiers of the Lord bearing the Lord Christ as their true arrow, and they say: "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Eph 6:13).

10.2.3.en: As for His saying: "out of him every oppressor speedily", it points to His work in His Church, which receives Him as the cornerstone, the nail, and the spiritual bow, for He removes from her the oppressor and the corrupter, so that all in her may be sanctified by Him.

10.3.0.en: Second: "And they shall be as mighty men, which tread down their enemies in the mire of the streets in the battle: and they shall fight, because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses shall be confounded" [5]. This is their might and this is their victory, that they tread down the mire of the streets, and so they are not like the one who had the talent and buried it in the earth (Mt 25:18); rather, by the heavenly Lord they rise above every material thought, soaring in the heavenly places, however violent this thought may appear, like riders on horses.

10.3.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind distinguishes between riders on horses and horsemen. The riders on horses are those who mount them without controlling them with a bridle; if the horses signify the body, then the soul mounts the body and leaves it in its wildness and stubbornness, so this soul is put to shame because of the lusts of the flesh. The horses also signify arrogant sophistic thoughts which the soul mounts, and so falls into pride and is deprived of salvation. Of the riders on horses it was said: "the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea" (Ex 15:1), "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God" (Ps 20:7), "An horse is a vain thing for safety" (Ps 33:7). This is concerning the riders on horses; but the horsemen signify him who mounts the horse or the steed and controls it with a bridle, for it was said to Elijah the prophet: "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof" (2 Kgs 2:12).

10.4.0.en: Third: He compensates them for the years that the locust had eaten; for instead of the losses that befell them on the day the Lord rejected them they receive great blessings which cover the former losses, for He says: "And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the LORD their God, and will hear them" [6]. Why does He speak of the house of Judah and the house of Joseph? Because from the first house came forth Jesus, the giver of salvation, and from the second house appeared Joseph, a type of Christ, who provided wheat after hunger and famine had crushed them (Gen 41:56). If Israel passed through years of famine, the true Joseph satisfies them, as the holy Mary said: "He hath filled the hungry with good things" (Lk 1:53). He is the Lord their God who answers their petition and satisfies their needs, so they no longer remember the past with its harsh spiritual famine, for the joys of the present cover all the sorrows of the past. Therefore He says: "And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine" [7]. This is the mark of the messianic age: the joy of the Holy Spirit, which the world cannot take away from the heart!

10.4.1.en: Here He mentions Ephraim as a mighty man full of joy, perhaps referring to the northern kingdom, which lived in captivity for a longer time than Judah, so He affirmed His support for it. Or perhaps He meant the tribe of Ephraim in particular because it was the violent one which was the first instigator of the corruption of the northern kingdom, especially as Jeroboam, who incited the ten tribes to revolt against Judah, was an Ephraimite (1 Kgs 11:26; 12:2), and he it was who established idol worship in Israel (1 Kgs 12:25-33). Now the Lord assures Ephraim that he will become a mighty man spiritually and his heart will be filled with joy.

10.5.0.en: Fourth: He gathers their dispersion and increases them in His bosom: "I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them: and they shall increase as they have increased" [8]. He is like the beekeeper who whistles to his scattered bees to gather honey from the meadows and gardens. He gathers them to Himself and gives them by blessing to grow and multiply as they had formerly multiplied, meaning that if He cared for them while they were under discipline, under the slavery of Pharaoh, so that they grew in proportion as they were afflicted (Ex 1:7), will He not much more make them grow and multiply when He redeems them from slavery?!

10.5.1.en: He fulfils in them His promise to Abraham, father of the fathers: "for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee" (Gen 17:5-6), and as it was said in Isaiah: "A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation" (Isa 60:22). And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [If these words were taken literally they would seem difficult, for many of the saints had no children at all, such as Elijah and Elisha and John the Baptist, than whom none attained greater virtue and knowledge of the holy mysteries (Mt 11:11), and yet he had no children, so we must understand this spiritually]. So on the one hand they have children in the Spirit, like those whom Paul begot in the Gospel (1 Cor 4:15), for whom he travailed until Christ be formed in them (Gal 4:19), or those whom the Apostle Peter calls "obedient children" (1 Pet 1:14), and on the other hand they have children in the heart, that is, the fruits of the Holy Spirit manifested in us as children who gladden the heart of God!

10.6.0.en: Fifth: When He brings them back to Himself to grow and bear fruit by the Holy Spirit, He sows them again among the peoples like living seed buried in the ground to bring forth much fruit, for He says: "And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again. I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them. And he shall pass through the sea with affliction, and shall smite the waves in the sea, and all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away. And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the LORD" [9-12].

10.6.1.en: What a living and joyful picture of God's work in them! After He gathers them from the captivity of sin and returns them to Himself, He casts them like living seed among the peoples to bear witness to salvation in far countries and to have spiritual children in the Lord. But they do not walk in the spirit of the world; rather, their hearts return from the symbolic land of Egypt, that is, the love of the world, and the Lord gathers them out of Assyria, that is, from the spirit of pride, and goes with them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and lest this be understood materially He said: "and place shall not be found for them", for they are in a state of continual migration and constant departure from strength to strength and from glory to glory, their hearts lifted up in the heavenly places, with no place for them on earth!

10.6.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on this phrase as a declaration of the spiritual migration of the believing man: [He who passes from vice to virtue. This is truly a change of country, a change from sin to righteousness, from evil to godliness... and goes from virtue to virtue (Ps 83:8), and passes from the shadow of the Law, where the letter kills, to reach the Spirit who gives life (2 Cor 3:6)]... St. Didymus sees that the migration to the spiritual Lebanon is a migration to a state of deification, that is, enjoying the attributes of the Lord Jesus, where the soul enters the glorious holy Church which has "not spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing" (Eph 5:27), so that it is said of her: "the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon" (Song 4:11).

10.7.0.en: When He brings them into the new Lebanon, that is, the holy life of the Church, He passes with them through the sea of affliction, like the living fish that hides in the water with all its disturbances and the sea with all its waves without losing its life... They enter into affliction in this world, but the waves of the world cannot swallow them up, nor the deeps of the river draw them down! Rather they come out of every affliction stronger, declaring the Kingdom of God within them, and so He concludes His discourse on the blessings of this age by saying: "And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the LORD" [12].

11.0.s.en: 1. A lament over those who rejected:

11.0.0.en: 1 Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. 2 Howl, fir tree; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are spoiled: howl, O ye oaks of Bashan; for the forest of the vintage is come down. 3 There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is spoiled: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is spoiled.

11.0.1.en: Israel's rejection of the Lord Christ turned it into total ruin, and so the prophet laments over it, saying: "Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. Howl, fir tree; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are struck: howl, O ye oaks of Bashan; for the forest of the vintage is come down. There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is spoiled: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is spoiled" [1-3].

11.0.3.en: First: that the ruin carries extended and comprehensive dimensions, striking Lebanon and Bashan and the Jordan, as though the Jews' rejection of the Lord Christ brought them under an extended, almost collective blow, for they cried out "His blood be on us, and on our children." And the comprehensiveness is not limited to places but includes kinds of trees: cedars burned with fire, the fir tree howling, and also the oak, and the trees of the forest falling, etc...

11.0.4.en: Second: He calls upon nature to grieve over the man who denied his Creator and rejected His saving work and even betrayed Him for thirty pieces of silver.

11.0.5.en: Third: what is mentioned here was fulfilled literally, for it was the custom of enemies, when they took possession of a fertile land such as the land of promise, to cut down its trees to make use of their wood, or to burn them with fire with the intention of destruction and devastation.

11.0.6.en: Fourth: from the symbolic side, to what does Lebanon point in His saying: "Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars"? The enemies entered Lebanon through its doors, that is, through the mountain passes leading to the city, in order to destroy its cedars of which it is proud. We saw Lebanon spiritually in the previous chapter as pointing to the migration to the holy Church to bear in us the sweet fragrance of Christ, so that it is said: "the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon" (Song 4:11). And as Lebanon points to the fruitful Church bearing the attributes of the Lord and His fragrance and the fruit of His Holy Spirit, so on the other hand, as St. Didymus the Blind says, it points to idolatry (apostasy from the faith) and arrogance, for he says: [Indeed, when the Bridegroom in the Song of Songs calls the Church of the victors He says to her: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse (Song 4:8)... she comes to the One who calls her from ignorance and unbelief to holy knowledge and perfect faith].

11.0.7.en: Fifth: what befalls the cedar, the fir, the oak, and the forest points to the Jewish communities that rejected the Messiah the Savior, and also to the sins that lie within the soul, driving a man to be deprived of the enjoyment of salvation. St. Didymus the Blind sees in the lofty cedar a reference to the company of the proud or to the demon of pride, for he says: [It is written in Isaiah against these barren, unfruitful trees: "For the day of the LORD of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low" (Isa 2:12), and a little later He says: "And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan" (Zech 2:13). These wild trees grow on pride... they will be eaten by the fire of the corrupt and diligent, as Isaiah himself says: "and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one" (Isa 10:34)]. St. Didymus also sees that if the cedar points to the pride of the great, then the fir, which is a small tree, points to those subject to them; if the cedar points to those who are wise and prudent in their own eyes, then the fir points to those who walk in their stream. Therefore when the fire devours the cedar the fir howls at the fall of the mighty who are their masters in their eyes.

11.0.8.en: As for the oak of Bashan, it points to the dense forests full of leafy trees which are without fruit, and they represent the hypocrites who have the appearance of religion and deny the power thereof. And the forest is the tree found in the wilderness, also without fruit!

11.0.9.en: Sixth: the prophet turns in his discourse to the shepherds who left their pastoral work and howl because the young lions roar to devour and there is none to deliver, and because the Jordan with its pride, on account of the dense forests and the trees in which the beasts hide, is spoiled.

11.0.10.en: This is the broad outline of the lament which the prophet laid upon every soul that rejects the work of salvation in it: its doors open before the enemy so that it loses all its trees, nature grieves over it, and eternal spiritual ruin comes upon it.

11.1.0.en: 4 Thus saith the LORD my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter; 5 Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not. 6 For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the LORD: but, lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.

11.1.1.en: "Thus saith the LORD my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter; whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not" [4-5].

11.1.2.en: Since they rejected the Messiah, the Lamb slain for themselves, they were given over to perdition and destruction. By their rejection of salvation they became worthless, their owners slay them and it is not counted against them as sin since they deserve to be slaughtered; and if their owner sells them he is relieved of them since they were a burden to him, so at the sale he says: Blessed be the Lord, I am rich. Perhaps by this He portrays for us the state of the Jews after they rejected the Savior, for they were scattered in many lands and exposed to bitter persecutions, each nation wishing to be rid of them as a burden upon them.

11.1.3.en: It is remarkable that God permits the wicked to have harsh shepherds for their discipline, for He says: "their own shepherds pity them not." The shepherds are from God, for when He is pleased with His people He says: "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding" (Jer 3:15), that is, they provide them with pastures of knowledge and understanding or pastures of divine wisdom which are from God (Eph 4:11; 1 Cor 12:28); but when He is angry with His people He leaves them to themselves, so they feed in the pastures of "the wisdom of this world" (1 Cor 2:6), and He gives them over to the pasture of "a reprobate mind" (Rom 1:28), and the pasture of "vile affections" (Rom 1:26).

11.1.4.en: Good shepherds lead the flock to the bosom of God and they enjoy security, but the wicked drive them out from God and they perish, therefore the psalmist says: "For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that go a whoring from thee. But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works" (Ps 73:27).

11.2.0.en: They rejected the good Shepherd, the Messiah the Savior, and so were deprived even of good shepherds, and the Lord gave them over to shepherds who have no pity on the flock... since He Himself no longer has pity on them, for He says: "For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the LORD: but, lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them" [6]. He called them "the inhabitants of the land", for they rejected the heavenly Messiah who came to lift them up from earth to heaven, so they remained with their hearts on the earth and were counted "inhabitants of the land" and even bore in themselves the nature of the earth. This earthy nature bears neither heavenly love nor largeness of heart, but each man delivers his brother to affliction and injustice for his destruction.

11.3.0.en: 7 And I will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock. And I took unto me two staves; the one I called Grace, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock. 8 Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me. 9 Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another. 10 And I took my staff, even Grace, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people. 11 And it was broken in that day: and so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the LORD.

11.3.1.en: It was the custom anciently for the shepherd to hold two staves, with the one he strikes any beast of prey that attacks the flock and with the other he leads the flock so that it does not stray from the way; but the Lord appears here holding two staves, namely: Grace or beauty, and Bands or union, so He leads us by His grace in His green heavenly pastures that we may lack nothing, and leads us by union so as to bind us all together in Him by the Spirit of divine love.

11.3.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that God by these two staves leads the Jews as well as the Gentiles as a rational flock, and the two staves also point to His work as Savior and as King.

11.4.0.en: In any case, by the Jews' rejection of the Messiah the King, the Lord cut asunder the staff of Grace, so they were deprived of divine help and lost His blessings because they broke His covenant. By this they lost His compassionate care: "Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another" [9], not out of contempt for the flock but out of His sanctifying of human freedom, so He left them to themselves, by themselves, from His grace.

11.4.1.en: He says: "Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me" [8]. Who are these three shepherds whom the Lord destroyed and the Jews lost? St. Jerome sees that these three are Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, who died shortly before the people entered the promised land. Perhaps he means that by their rejection of the Lord Christ they lost His threefold care as priest, king, and giver of prophecy, so they were deprived of His atoning intercession (His priesthood) and of His kingship as a leader who conquers and brings them into victory, and of the giver of prophecy who reveals to them the mysteries of the life to come. In ancient times the king was other than the priest and other than the seer or prophet, but in Christ these three were combined on a superior and unique level.

11.5.0.en: 12 And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. 13 And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the LORD. 14 Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

11.5.1.en: God did not wish to present this dark picture of what befell the people of the circumcision because of their rejection of the Messiah without disclosing the form of this rejection in the act of betrayal committed by Judas against his Master for thirty pieces of silver, which represents the betrayal of the whole people, for they valued Him at the price of a slave deserving death.

11.5.2.en: "And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter in the house of the LORD" [12-13].

11.5.3.en: First: what is the silver that was offered as the price for the betrayal of the Lord? St. Didymus the Blind says: [Let us take the wages and the silver from the spiritual side. Silver often points to divine knowledge and the divine word, as in the saying: "The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times" (Ps 12:6), and in Proverbs it says: "The tongue of the just is as choice silver" (Prov 10:2). Here the word "tongue" means "speech". But not every "silver" word is taken in a good sense, for the Lord says of the erring priests of the Jews: "Thy silver is become dross" (Isa 1:22). Here He does not accuse the silver itself but their deceitful speech, and the Lord says of those who utter this speech: "Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them" (Jer 6:3), for He rejected those who deceive out of zeal and those who break the commandments. In the same way we understand what was said in Proverbs, that the silver given for deceit must be taken as a piece of earthenware (Prov 26:23); this is the speech of those who care only for earthly things (the earthen pottery), of whom it was said in Isaiah: "their voice comes from the ground" (Isa 8:19). So there are kinds of silver, for when the people of the circumcision determined thirty pieces of silver as the wage for Him who suffered for their sake (Mt 20:28; Mk 10:5; Jn 10:15)... they paid counterfeit silver... offering deceitful speech. And in Christianity also there are people whose beliefs are wrong, "walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully" (2 Cor 4:2), who understand the word of God according to their own desires. Of these we must beware and count their discourses as counterfeit silver].

11.5.4.en: As if the Jews and the heretics, in offering deceitful and misleading words, sell the Lord for counterfeit silver!

11.5.5.en: Second: they counted Him a slave, so they paid the price, thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave (Ex 21:32). Perhaps the number 30 symbolizes the defilement of the five senses, for if the number 6 points to deficiency, then the number 5 (the senses) multiplied by 6 produces 30. As if the price of betraying the Lord Christ is the defilement of our senses for the benefit of His enemy the devil instead of sanctifying them to Him.

11.5.6.en: Third: what does he mean by the potter to whom the silver was cast in the house of the Lord? St. Didymus the Blind sees that the counterfeit silver paid as the price of the Lord Christ for His betrayal meets in the house of Holy Scripture, which is the house of the potter, where the testing fire exposes their deceptions and reveals their contradiction with the prophecies concerning the Lord.

11.5.7.en: Fourth: since the potter deals with dust and clay and with fire, the casting of the silver into the potter's house declares the nature of their earthy, earthly heart, which is not fit to be placed in palaces or treasuries but in the dust.

11.5.8.en: Fifth: with this price a field was bought called "the field of blood", used for burying strangers (Mt 27:7), pointing to the acceptance of the Gentiles, where we are buried with Christ at the price of His blood to rise with Him. St. Jerome says: [The price of Christ is the place of our burial, and the field was called "a field of blood"; it is the field of the blood of the Jews but it is the place of our burial, for we are strangers and foreigners and have no place of rest. He was crucified and died and we were buried with Him].

11.6.0.en: Sixth: he concludes his discourse on the rejection of the Messiah and their betrayal of Him by saying: "Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands (union), that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel" [14]. St. Didymus the Blind sees that the two staves will come together and be united as one staff, as in (Ezek 37), when the Jews return at the end of the ages and accept the Lord Christ, and so become one with Judah (the Church of the New Testament) by entering the faith.

11.7.0.en: 15 And the LORD said unto me, Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd. 16 For, lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek the young one, nor heal that that is broken, nor feed that that standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their claws in pieces. 17 Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened."

11.8.0.en: Since they rejected the Lord Christ, the good Shepherd, they were deprived of divine grace and of union together in the Lord by the cutting of the two staves, and they accepted the false shepherding of the Antichrist, for He says: "Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd. For, lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek the young one, nor heal that that is broken, nor feed that that standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their claws in pieces" [16].

11.8.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on this phrase, saying: [God, who leaves them in their shame, raised up for them a foolish shepherd without experience in shepherding, who destroys those who chose him as their shepherd. He does not care for the stray one who has gone far off alone from the flock to bring it back, who separated by its straying. He does not preserve anything, and does not seek those who were scattered, and does not tend the wounded, and does not lead the healthy. His aim is evil and not for good, he runs after his own advantage and his greed and devours the flesh and tears off the claws of those under his care. He is not like the shepherds whom God gives, saying: "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding" (Jer 3:15). For can they be anything but good shepherds who have as their head Him who gives His life for the sheep as the good Shepherd (Jn 10:15)...? For it was said: "And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away" (1 Pet 5:4). Those who shepherd the sheep in this way do not lord it over those who are their charge (1 Pet 5:3), but those who eat the flesh of the sheep seek their own pleasure, thinking they find glory in the shame of their deeds. They eat without discernment, so their god is their belly (Phil 3:19) and they are slaves to it and not slaves of Christ Jesus. Of these the Apostle writes: "they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly" (Rom 16:18)].

11.8.2.en: What does He mean by tearing off the claws? Good shepherds keep "the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Eph 4:3), but the wicked tear off from the flock its claws as they are torn from fingers, that is, they cause it to lose its unity.

11.9.0.en: This is the fruit of the people's evil: the Lord leaves them to a foolish shepherd who scatters them as he scatters himself, for He says: "Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened" [17]. And as St. Didymus the Blind says of this sword which breaks the arm of the foolish shepherd and his right eye: [The word of God threatens especially the unfaithful shepherds... So the Lord says in Isaiah: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword" (Isa 1:19-20), as He also speaks in Jeremiah of the avenging sword: "for I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land" (Jer 6:12) that they may perish... The avenging sword is upon the arm of (the foolish shepherd) and his eye, that is, it touches the senses of action and contemplation, so his arm dries up as it becomes a dead member, and his right eye is struck with blindness...].

11.9.1.en: St. Didymus sees in this prophecy a reference to the Antichrist who has a strong arm through the signs he performs (2 Thess 2:9), while his right eye points to his intellectual deceptions as he claims perfect knowledge though he is a liar (1 Tim 6:20), and Elymas the sorcerer bore a type of him, who deceived by his magical works and his lies, so his works were nullified and he was struck with blindness, not seeing the sun (Acts 13:10).
